value.rationale: Two natural nonisomorphic 2-covers of the Petersen graph reveal a quantitative inversion between count of equilibria and total fixed-point attraction. The Desargues graph has two 388-state shore equilibria while the dodecahedral graph has no fixed-point basin over 35. These exact selection-basin invariants are natural dynamics statistics, previously not implied by known generic NOR orbit restrictions or MIS counts, and support comparative work on network topology and attraction.
